'''''Pterocephalus lasiospermus''''' ('''rosalillo de cumbre''') is a [[species]] of [[shrub]] in the family [[Caprifoliaceae]].

== Etymology ==
'''lasiospermus''': ''lasios'' from the Greek, meaning "hairy" and ''sperma'', meaning "seed", referring to it [[Pappus (flower structure)|pappus]].<ref>{{cite book |author=A. J. L. Jourdan |title=Dictionnaire raisonné, étymologique, synonymique et polyglote, des termes usités dans les sciences naturelles |publisher=Société Belge de Librairie  |year=1837 |page=349 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xdz1-kpYaHMC&pg=PA349}}</ref>
The Spanish common name means "summit rosebush" in English.

== Geographic distribution ==
Endemic to Cañadas del Teide depression on [[Tenerife]] and the scrub  of the upper zones of the surrounding pine forest. Before the creation of the [[Teide National Park]] it was very scarce due to the damage from livestock pasturing.<ref>{{cite report|date=2006 |title=Proposal to inscribe Teide National Park on the World Heritage List | page=54 |url=http://reddeparquesnacionales.mma.es/en/parques/teide/patrimonio/patrimonio_indice.htm}}</ref>

== Description ==
Form is a shrub up to one meter in height. Its stems are grey, with simple leaves of pale green-grey, both are hairy.<ref>[http://tenerife-ecologia.blogspot.com.es/2011/10/rosalillo-de-cumbre-pterocephalus.html Tenerife-ecología]</ref> The [[inflorescence]] is a cushion-like head of pale pink flowers at the end of long [[Plant stem|stem]]s.<ref>{{cite book |author=David Bramwell, Zoë I. Bramwell |title=Wild Flowers of the Canary Islands |publisher=Rueda |location=Madrid |year=2001 |page=321 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dhM8PwAACAAJ}}</ref> It blooms in early summer, which is late with respect to other species in its environment. As summer progresses, the [[flower]] head becomes a ball of whitish [[chaff]]y [[seed]]s.
